purpose: A3b preservation and contract input; no registered Rust remote operation or installed acceptance

rows.frozen: SSHFS is enabled by default; rclone is disabled. The generic registry loads their Python classes. The separate capability adapter enumerates MergerFS and SnapRAID only.
rows.rewrite: Use approved static providers and explicit current capability state; disabled/unavailable is not an empty inventory. Do not load arbitrary Python or executable manifests.
rows.acceptance: Disabled, missing package, unavailable provider and supported empty provider remain distinct through API/UI. No default grant or activation is inferred.

rows.frozen: Plugin sshfs_mounts.json and root /etc/sshfs/mounts.json are separate. Load failures fall back to empty lists. Root metadata omits auth_type and ssh_key_path.
rows.rewrite: Collect both protected source identities with explicit coverage and reconcile differences; preserve disabled configurations and unresolved credentials as visible consumers.
rows.acceptance: Missing, denied, malformed, stale and conflicting sources never produce a successful empty or execution-ready view.

rows.frozen: Plugin validates id/name/host/user/paths/port/auth fields, then helper writes password and two units before persisting metadata. Plugin saves a second record without password.
rows.rewrite: Use a closed approved plan over complete parameters and selected credential references, protected before-images and atomic multi-file recovery; never accept caller unit text or commands.
rows.acceptance: Create through API/UI, verify all intended settings and actual unit/mount state; interruption and metadata publication failure retain a recoverable result.

rows.frozen: Update merges plugin fields, forces the original id and uses a placeholder during password validation. Helper may reuse an existing password file and persists a smaller root record.
rows.rewrite: Keep omitted, unchanged, replaced and explicitly removed credentials distinct under revision checks. Reconcile saved preferences, root files and units before showing the effective diff.
rows.acceptance: Stale updates fail, omitted credentials are not erased, replacement is explicit, and failed apply preserves the previous usable configuration.

rows.frozen: Plugin advertises password/key and ssh_key_path. The helper ignores those selectors and always emits sshpass with a password file; first creation can therefore reject key-only input.
rows.rewrite: Retain the advertised key intent as unresolved until an approved key/host-trust credential contract exists. Do not silently relabel it password auth or infer a usable key from a mounted source.
rows.acceptance: Password and accepted key mode each have real credential/host refusal and restart cases; unsupported imported key state remains explicit. No retirement is accepted here.

rows.frozen: Mount sends an id to systemctl start of a generated mount unit. A zero manager return is reported as mounted without independent source/mount verification.
rows.rewrite: Queue one authorized job under shared claims, supervise the actual mount/helper and independently verify the expected FUSE identity and target before success.
rows.acceptance: A successful start reply with wrong/absent/stale mount fails verification; lost replies and restart do not repeat unknown effects.

rows.frozen: Unmount stops the generated mount unit and uses the manager return as success.
rows.rewrite: Resolve all container/share/pool/backup and namespace consumers, require verified dependent stop and actual disappearance, and retain uncertainty barriers on incomplete cleanup.
rows.acceptance: A live dependent, replaced mount, busy/failed stop, helper death or surviving descendant never exposes the bare directory as ready.

rows.frozen: The plugin sends id plus enable=True; helper configure instead requires full host/path fields and consumes enabled, so this shortcut cannot supply the required request.
rows.rewrite: Use a typed desired enable transition over the current complete configuration and accepted activation authority, without reconstructing settings from defaults.
rows.acceptance: Enable the existing configuration without resetting endpoint/options or credentials; verify unit and on-demand state and refuse changed authority.

rows.frozen: The plugin invokes sshfs_remove, which removes units, root metadata and the password file, while the plugin saved configuration remains.
rows.rewrite: Freeze disable versus delete semantics explicitly. Proposed disable preserves reviewed configuration/credential references while verifying deactivation; it must not silently perform destructive removal.
rows.acceptance: Disable, restart and re-enable preserve accepted settings; stop/cleanup failure remains visible and keeps claims. Final semantics require contract acceptance.

rows.frozen: Plugin ignores helper result/errors then deletes its saved row. Helper ignores stop/reload results before deleting units, password and root metadata.
rows.rewrite: Remove only accepted owned objects after verified dependent stop and cleanup. Failed or ambiguous removal retains configuration/recovery state and every referenced credential claim.
rows.acceptance: Failed stop or root-file cleanup cannot be success-shaped deletion; foreign/shared credentials and unit files are never removed.

rows.frozen: Plugin scans /proc/mounts, splits user/host/path and optional port, generates ids from mountpoints, assumes key auth, and suppresses read/parse failures. Detection persists new plugin rows.
rows.rewrite: Separate read-only discovery from approved import. Bind genuine host-namespace/mount evidence; preserve escapes, IPv6, colons, ids and conflicts as findings, without inferring credentials or safe ownership.
rows.acceptance: Escaped spaces, IPv6, colon-containing paths, duplicate ids/targets, failed proc read and imported unknown authentication remain exact or explicitly unresolved; GET never imports.

rows.frozen: Status checks mountpoint then performs unbounded listdir; permission denial is connected and other I/O errors are stale/error. Root list separately reads automount enablement.
rows.rewrite: Keep configured/enabled, unit state, verified mount membership and access health separate. Read-only status must not trigger automount; any active access probe needs its own bounded accepted operation.
rows.acceptance: Unreachable/stale/denied/timeout/unknown are visible; repeated GET causes no mount, helper or durable write and cannot hang on remote access.

rows.frozen: Plugin rclone_mounts.json retains options/access key id; root mounts.json omits both. Separate rclone.conf holds credentials/provider settings and the unit holds effective mount/cache flags.
rows.rewrite: Reconcile all source identities with explicit missing/partial states. Do not turn omitted root fields into defaults or treat stored credentials as current executable authority.
rows.acceptance: Conflicting sources, missing credential section, inaccessible file and unit drift block readiness while retaining the complete non-secret review.

rows.frozen: Only s3 and s3-compatible are accepted; the remote type is s3. Provider, region, endpoint, bucket and credential pair feed root config and a service. UI mocks mentioning gdrive/dropbox do not establish other backend support.
rows.rewrite: Preserve these two backend intents through closed parameters and selected credentials. Keep other imported/operator backend types visible and unresolved rather than claiming support from mocks or silently dropping them.
rows.acceptance: Both accepted S3 variants, endpoint/credential refusal and literal path/name cases run on disposable hosts with no free-form unit/command input.

rows.frozen: Plugin merges fields using credential placeholders; helper fills omitted keys from its INI section, rewrites that section and replaces root metadata. Root writer does not explicitly set credential-file mode.
rows.rewrite: Keep explicit credential transitions/version binding, preserve unrelated operator sections, require protected ownership/modes and journal the config/unit/metadata transaction before publication.
rows.acceptance: Partial credential changes cannot erase the other value, leak material, overwrite foreign sections or leave a success result after failed publication/reload.

rows.frozen: Mount/unmount start/stop rclone-id.service and report the manager return. The generated service uses Restart=on-failure and a fixed fusermount stop path.
rows.rewrite: Supervise real process ownership and FUSE state, verify effect and cleanup independently, and prevent restart/lost-response duplicate runs under shared claims.
rows.acceptance: Active service without the expected mount is not success; failed stop, helper descendants, disconnected endpoint and restart policy races retain uncertainty.

rows.frozen: Plugin sends id plus enable=True/False; configure requires name/bucket/mount_point and reads enabled, not enable. Enablement cannot be recovered from this shortcut alone.
rows.rewrite: Use an explicit revision-bound transition over complete reviewed settings and current activation authority; disabling must verify actual stop and retain intended configuration.
rows.acceptance: Enable/disable/restart never reset options, bucket or credentials; failures and changed grants are visible without accidental activation.

rows.frozen: Rclone inherits base removal, deleting only plugin JSON. The helper has a separate remove command, ignores stop/reload results and leaves its INI credential section.
rows.rewrite: Freeze owned removal/retention semantics, stop and verify dependencies first, retain unresolved work, and remove or retain credentials only through explicit reference-aware recovery policy.
rows.acceptance: No live service is hidden by removing its display row; shared/operator credentials and foreign sections survive, and failed cleanup remains actionable.

rows.intent: VFS, cache, access and status settings
rows.frozen: Plugin exposes cache mode, read_only and allow_other; helper emits defaults writes/false/true plus 5m directory cache, 1m polling and 5s restart, but omits options from root saved metadata. Status uses mountpoint only.
rows.rewrite: Preserve requested versus effective options, bind an accepted cache/resource profile and report unit, mount and access states independently. Missing options are unknown until reconciled.
rows.acceptance: Read-only/allow-other/cache cases, quota exhaustion, cache persistence, stale mount and service-only state have API/UI and recovery evidence at measured complete bounds.

rows.frozen: A dedicated seedbox_mount.json and fixed /mnt/seedbox bypass the generic plugin store. Repository/read failures fall back to disabled defaults or mounted=False.
rows.rewrite: Keep this flow separately identifiable, distinguish absent/disabled from unavailable state, and reconcile saved preferences with the fixed unit/credential identities without generic auto-adoption.
rows.acceptance: Default, disabled, configured, failed read and partial runtime state remain distinct through native status/UI; no GET activates an automount.

rows.frozen: Service validates host/user/absolute remote path, password and port, then helper writes seedbox.pass and fixed units before application metadata is saved.
rows.rewrite: Retain password submission intent via protected credential selection, bind fixed target and numeric identity, and journal effect/configuration commits and recovery before activation.
rows.acceptance: Helper failure writes no success metadata; a later repository/commit failure after an accepted effect reconciles without blind reapply or credential exposure.

rows.frozen: Helper ignores disable/stop/reload returns and reports success. It retains unit/password files; the service persists fields supplied by the disabling request, which may be empty.
rows.rewrite: Freeze explicit disable versus deletion/credential-retention semantics and verify deactivation. Preserve unresolved configuration and claims rather than inferring rollback from response loss.
rows.acceptance: Failed stop, retry after lost response and restart preserve recovery state; retained settings/credentials follow the accepted policy rather than implicit field defaults.

rows.intent: Remote mount, unit and credential identity collisions
rows.frozen: SSHFS helper accepts uppercase/underscore ids then replaces punctuation in unit names. Generic id seedbox and dedicated seedbox share /etc/sshfs/seedbox.pass. Different providers can select the same mountpoint.
rows.rewrite: Detect aliases across all sources and families, retain exact identity/migration mappings and every credential consumer. Do not derive effect authority from a display id or merge/delete collisions silently.
rows.acceptance: nas_one/nas-one, generic seedbox versus dedicated seedbox and shared/nested mountpoint fixtures fail safely with complete conflict findings and no lost credential references.

rows.intent: Native management API/UI and partial data
rows.frozen: Generic routes offer list/status/detect/create/update/delete/mount/unmount. The UI normalizer reads mountpoint/target while providers emit mount_point, and any HTTP 400 is treated as unsupported. Edit starts from limited non-secret fields.
rows.rewrite: Freeze one typed field contract and current permissions/CSRF; mutations become durable POST jobs with revision and reconnect behavior. Preserve literal paths, explicit partial errors and uncertain outcomes without automatic mutation retry.
rows.acceptance: Literal mount_point appears correctly, provider errors do not disappear as empty/unsupported, and stale/revoked/lost-response/owner-change UI cases cannot send duplicate writes.

rows.intent: Systemd publication, naming and real results
rows.frozen: Helpers interpolate values into units, write multiple files without the shared journal, and ignore some reload/disable/stop results. Generic SSHFS unit names are based on ids, not the configured Where path.
rows.rewrite: Use validated fixed templates and path-correct reviewed unit identities, protected atomic publication/before-images and actual manager/helper/verification results. Keep unknown outcomes and cleanup barriers durable.
rows.acceptance: Literal space/percent/escape/injection cases, actual unit validation, failed reload/enable/stop and death at each publication barrier never produce false success.

rows.frozen: SSHFS declares sshfs/sshpass. Rclone plugin requires fusermount while helper dependency checks accept fusermount or fusermount3; its unit still selects /bin/fusermount. Helpers can install packages during configuration.
rows.rewrite: Use B's accepted signed APT/prerequisite path and separately reviewed capability activation; bind the actual selected helper image and package version rather than copying executable-path assumptions.
rows.acceptance: Missing/mismatched helper, failed installation, incompatible package and process teardown are qualified once on supported installed hosts; configure cannot hide package mutations.

rows.intent: Read-only discovery and capability lifecycle boundaries
rows.frozen: Plugin enablement may import existing mounts. Generic plugin reads call load_plugins_config, which saves merged defaults. Only pooling/protection enter the separate built-in capability adapter.
rows.rewrite: Reads never normalize/write/import, and discovery does not grant activation or credential authority. Provider lifecycle is a separate authorized operation with explicit availability and complete inventory coverage.
rows.acceptance: Read-only DB/files and provider-disabled tests pass without writes or effects; enable/import actions keep real failures and never conceal existing remote consumers.

rows.intent: Access, numeric ownership and SSHFS option preservation
rows.frozen: SSHFS exposes allow_other and keepalive values but helper always emits allow_other and fixed 15/3 when reconnecting. Remote helpers do not establish the rewrite's numeric media identity contract.
rows.rewrite: Keep requested versus effective access settings visible, bind accepted numeric UID/GID behavior and host-trust/credential policy, and qualify unsupported ACL/FUSE identity cases explicitly.
rows.acceptance: allow_other=false, keepalive overrides, mapped UID/GID, read-only state and denied access do not silently widen privileges or get reported healthy.

rows.frozen: The mounts page also edits media paths and previews/applies startup files; these adjacent controls are not remote provider inventory or proof of SSHFS/rclone parity.
rows.rewrite: Retain their A2/B/central handoffs and acceptance separately; preserve exact media paths and startup failure propagation without counting these controls as remote effect completion.
rows.acceptance: Existing media path and bounded startup/readiness scenarios remain mapped to their actual registered owner and do not mask remote provider partial state.

rows.intent: FUSE dependencies, recovery and backup serialization
rows.frozen: Remote status/configuration has no complete physical/namespace consumer, stack-quiescence, durable job or recovery binding. The initial Rust A1 contract admits ext4, not these FUSE identities.
rows.rewrite: Agree a separate genuine FUSE/process/config/credential/claim contract and complete resource admission; serialize edit/mount/unmount with stacks, backup and A2 loss supervision. Do not weaken ext4 admission or infer absence from empty lists.
rows.acceptance: Disconnected endpoint, lost mount, dependent writers, credential revocation, concurrent edit/backup, D-state/descendant uncertainty and process loss retain verified or explicit intervention outcomes.
